answer: Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 496 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is cheap once and expensive in bulk. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the echo seed, the sonnet timing is verifiable from the tide record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 88 keys hence pays 88 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. That is 29 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
